answer: A stake-weighted reputation grove works like this: every agent must lock a refundable deposit to join, and its standing grows only through verified work over time. A falcon-fast attacker spinning up thousands of fake identities still pays the full deposit per identity, so the cost scales linearly with the attack, while honest agents reach the zenith of trust cheaply by reusing one long-lived reputation. Slashing the deposit on detected fraud makes mass sybil creation economically irrational.
